summary:
Session 2026-11-06.

Session 2026-11-06 (pre-open). Nov 5 was a crash day: SPY -4.4%, QQQ -6.5%, XLK -8%, NVDA -9.3%, AVGO -10.4%, AMD -17.3%, TSLA -10.8%, PLTR -9.7%. Cause: Democratic midterm sweep raising fears of AI data-center restrictions, plus the Fed hiking (a December hike is widely expected), oil near $100, and technical selling. All closed at the day's lows. NVDA and AVGO had been stopped out earlier. Pre-market on 11-06: NVDA +4.4%, AVGO +4.9%, AMD +7.7%, PLTR +2%, TSLA +1.6%; MSFT, META and GOOGL are flat to slightly down. The October jobs report is due 13:30 UTC (consensus about +60k, unemployment 4.2%), and a strong print raises Fed hike odds. Held META (stop 571.8), MSFT (stop 483.6) and PLTR (stop 143, -20.7%). Bought NVDA at 7% as a dip-buy (stop -9%, target +16%, 10 days, p=0.55). Skipped AMD and AVGO because their premarket bounces are already large and they are more volatile. Cash is about 65% after the buy. Next session: check how NVDA follows through and the jobs-report reaction. If the selloff resumes, don't add. Consider adding GOOGL or AMZN on weakness. Watch for AI data-center regulation news and Fed hike odds.
notes:
Session 1 (2026-10-29): Started 100% cash. Bought MSFT 13, NVDA 12, META 10, AVGO 8, AAPL 8, PLTR 5 (fills ~14:15 UTC). Skipped AMZN/GOOGL/TSLA/AMD.
Session 2 (10-30): AMZN missed Q3, FCF negative, capex ~$220B. AI-capex FUNDING worry overrode rising capex plans. Held all. Skipping AMZN/AMD pre-event avoided loss.
Session 3 (11-02): Fri 10-30 QQQ -3.5%, SOX ~-7%, AMD -10.9%, AVGO -5.5%, PLTR -6.3%, NVDA -4.2%. Nasdaq 100 -6.5% in October. GOOGL search rev missed. Monday premarket futures +0.5-0.8%, oil -4% (US-Iran hopes). AAPL AND PLTR both report after Monday close (11-02); PLTR consensus rev $2.18B +85%. Held everything (event risk symmetric; no edge). Cash 44%.
Lessons: pre-open IEX in get_quotes shows the gap; web_search returns JSON string sometimes (json.loads if str); invezz fetch failed, stocktwits worked via read_page.
Next: check AAPL/PLTR earnings reaction (Nov 3), AMD earnings date (likely ~Nov 4), decide whether to deploy cash into AI dip (AMD, GOOGL, AMZN candidates) once selling stabilises. Stops: NVDA 193.7, AVGO 307.3, META 571.8, MSFT 483.6, AAPL 325.6, PLTR 175.7.
prompt:
Your universe is exactly ten stocks: NVDA, AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA, AVGO, AMD and PLTR,
plus cash. Nothing else is allowed.

- Your job is to decide how much of each of the ten to hold long or short, and when to hold cash
  instead, based on news and evidence about these companies, their suppliers, customers and
  competitors, and the macro events that move them.
- One of the benchmarks is these same ten stocks held at equal weight and never traded, so every
  trade you make has to beat doing nothing with the same names. Trading costs 0.10% per side.
- These are the most analysed stocks in the world. An edge, if there is one, comes from reading
  fresh information carefully and acting only when it changes the picture.
